newsitem.title: ROMANIA: EBRD pledges $200 mln loan for Romtelecom.
newsitem.headline: EBRD pledges $200 mln loan for Romtelecom.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development has agreed to give Romania's Romtelecom RA telephone utility a $200 million loan to fund its development and privatisation plans, the government said.

The EBRD signed a letter of intent in Bucharest on Friday, saying it would release the funds after state-run Romtelecom launches its privatisation programme aimed at turning it into a shareholding company, the government said in a statement.
Pantis also said his ministry had decided to give a potential strategic investor in Romtelecom less than 51 percent in the company along with management posts.
EBRD is also expected to call a tender to designate an international consultant to evaluate Romtelecom.

Romania's privatisation programme, launched in 1992 after delays, has so far failed to deal with large utilities, including Romtelecom, which form the core of the economy and offer the best hope of attracting big foreign investment.
Privatisation of Romtelecom, which has the monopoly on telephone services in Romania, could attract up to $4.0 billion, official estimates say.
The utility currently employs 55,000 people and has some 2.8 million subscribers across the Balkan country.
In 1992 the EBRD gave Romtelecom a credit of 142 million ECUs to instal a fibre optic telecommunications network.
